Magic Mushrooms

By: Michael Duffett | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
Psychoactive mushrooms have been used in religious ceremonies for 100’s of

years. Monica Kromhout who used to run Life Line and is an astrologer faces 15

years in prison for being caught holding mushroom ceremonies in Cape Town.

She is defying police and continues to hold these ceremonies.

More and more research is coming out to show the healing properties of magic

mushrooms, and in the program we will interview a CNN reporter had had ptsd

after spending years in war torn countries. She underwent mushroom therapy

and was cured of her ailments. In the war against drugs, mushrooms have been

lumped with drugs such as crack and cocaine.

The story will feature the arrest of Monica and we will speak to people who feel

that many of their symptoms have been cured through the use of the

mushrooms. We will film a ceremony and also hear from a psychiatrist who also

participates in these ceremonies. It’s expected that this case may go all the way

to the constitutional court.

Press Release:


Magic Mushrooms
Capetonian Monica Cromhout regularly breaks the law. She’s been holding illegal mushroom ceremonies at her home for several years. Psychotropic mushrooms are banned in South Africa and elsewhere and classed with other hard drugs. Yet, participants in her Soma (spirit of the mushroom) ceremonies and others who use so-called psilocybin, report remarkable health benefits. Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


Magic Mushrooms Script

For millennia indigenous people have used various means to access the spirit world, one being through the use of psilocybin, commonly known as magic mushrooms. Such ceremonies still take place in the modern world, and locally in Cape Town.

Monica: (Sound Up) How many grams tonight?

Monica Cromhout carefully weighs and hands out psilocybin to participants in her so-called Soma Ceremonies. Soma means the spirit of the mushroom.

Monica, who earns a living as an astrologer, has spent her life helping and caring for people. She has worked as nurse and was also director of Life Line. But her life was to change irrevocably.

LINK
IT WAS ON THIS SPOT THAT MONICA HAD HER FIRST EXPERIENCE WITH MUSHROOMS. IT WAS ALSO THE FIRST TIME SHE SAYS SHE HEARD THE VOICE OF THE SPIRIT OF THE MUSHROOMS.

Psilocybin is a banned substance in terms of the drug and drug trafficking act as it is psychedelic drug. Users experience a dream-like state and changes in perception. It’s used recreationally by some and also at music festivals world wide to enhance the experience. But it is also known as an entheogen – a substance that evokes spiritual awakening.

Monica: It goes beyond words because you go into symbols and archetypes and sounds and feelings and awareness that are just exploding.

LINK
69-YEAR-OLD MONICA CROMHOUT HAS BEEN HOLDING MUSHROOM CEREMONIES HERE IN SOMERSET WEST CAPE TOWN FOR THE PAST 6 YEARS. NOT IN HER WILDEST IMAGINATION DID SHE EVER BELIEVE THAT HER LIFE WOULD FOLLOW THIS PATH.

It’s a path, she says, that she discovered after her first experience with psyocbolin.

Monica: This voice instructed me, told me actually that my home would become a school for mushrooms.

Hundreds of Capetonians, including doctors, attorneys, and musicians have been attending these ceremonies. She knew she was breaking the law and it caught up with her in December last year.

John: So you said that you always anticipated the police possibly coming around.
Monica: I knew, I try not to anticipate it but I knew it was a possibility
John: And ‘lo and behold’ that is precisely what happened one night.
Monica: In the most extraordinary of ways.
John: Tell us about it.
An elderly man attending a ceremony became confused and paranoid. He slipped away unseen by Monica’s minders who oversee each participant .

Monica: I was really worried about him. Really worried because I could imagine how frightened he must be.

A search party was sent out, including the local neighborhood watch but to no avail. The man ended up at the local police station two kilometers away and asked to be taken back. A contingent of armed police descended onto Monica’s home. She was initially thrilled.

Monica: You've got Peter! You've found peter! And they said yes we have but they had left him in the front and behind those two came a whole lot more. About eight more policemen.

Remarkably the police did not interfere with the group who were still in the midst of their journey, but they did search Monica’s house. They found 2 kilograms of mushrooms in a fridge and arrested her for dealing, which carries a heavy jail sentence. That she spent two nights in the holding cells concerned her attorney Name and Surname? Took out the bedroom bit to make space for his name and surbame

Attorney: We have certain rules and procedures in place when we arrest, for example, a minor, and I don’t understand why the same courtesy couldn’t have been applied to a lady of her age.

Monica received hundreds messages of support from around the world during her incarceration including one from Valentina Leo, a teacher of sacred sexuality, as well as an artistic director who designed the show experience of Madam Zingara.

Valentina: Monica is a gift because she is an elder. There is something so precious when you meet an elder person that have journeyed through their whole lives and now they choose what they know to be true.

The late advocate Robin Stransham-Ford felt the same and visited her in the police cells.

Monica: I was a bit suspicious actually because my mind was saying, "I can't afford this."

But the advocate heavily discounted his services. After getting Monica bail, he set about petitioning the high court to halt proceedings. He planned to take the matter to the constitutional court and argue that psilocybin was not addictive, had beneficial effects and that it should be decriminalized. But he died a few months later of terminal cancer.

Dr. Mike West who works in the Division of Addiction Psychiatry at Groote Schuur Hospital says that psilocybin is not physically addictive but can be psychologically which means there is still a risk of addiction or dependency. His research only uncovered three deaths attributed to the ingestion of psilocybin alone. Lawyers asked for the red bit to be added in

Dr. West: Indirect deaths have been reported. Generally due to disturbances in behavior, self harm or associated with multiple drugs ingestion.

Psychedelics like psilocybin and LSD were used in the 1960s in experimental research to treat mental health disorders but as their popularity grew amongst recreational users, they were reclassified as controlled substances as America declared war on drugs.

Dr. West: This had the result of preventing scientists from continuing their research into the potential uses of these substances.

Psilocybin acts on neural circuits in the brain that use the neurotransmitter serotonin. There has recently been a resurgence of studies.

LINK
MORE AND MORE RESEARCH IS BEING DONE ON THE POSITIVE EFFECTS OF PSILOCYBIN. IT IS ALREADY BEING USED TO TREAT A RANGE OF CONDITIONS FROM PTSD, TO ANXIETY, DEPRESSION AND EVEN SOME ADDICTIONS.

So convinced of its healing potential and spiritual benefits, Monica, despite the court case hanging over her head, is continuing to hold her ceremonies.

Monica: I have a responsibility. I am a very responsible person and my sense of responsibility goes beyond the law.

She spends the whole day preparing for the event. She addresses participants and tells them what to expect. She claims she makes no money from these events - The R700 she charges are for the mushrooms and to pay her helpers. A trip or journey takes about 5 hours, and each user’s experience is different


Lady: A lot of the times it is very painful and as the emotions come up for you. Hurt, sadness, a lot of crying.

Marlene’s describes the journey as an evolution.
Lady: As it turns it becomes beautiful then you filled. You filled with so much love. You actually just want to hug the planet, hold the planet. Everybody is beautiful in your eyes.

Monica feeds the group after their trip at about midnight and everybody sleeps until morning before a debriefing at breakfast.

According to American research, 67% of healthy volunteers who participated in a psilocybin study rated their experience to be either the single most meaningful experience of their lives or amongst the top 5. This was Valentina's experience when she, as she calls it, ingested the sacrament at one ceremony.

Valentina: When the medicine really starts to open, it’s opening like a flower. You feel layers of your being dissolving, you letting go the edges of your being and the deep space inside of you start to express. I met the place of love. The true place of love where everything was perfect.

John: Once you have emerged from that state, is it something that stays with you?

Valentina: Totally, totally. I mean the experience unfortunately not. Not to that extent when you are into the journey but the teaching yes. The teaching yes completely.

But users can experience side effects such as headaches, dizziness, nausea, anxiety and paranoia.

Dr. West: In even rarer cases psilocybin ingestion has been associated with a new onset of psychosis in people that were potentially predisposed to developing it.

Dr. Mike West does not condone psilocybin use of it and stresses that it is particularly dangerous for certain people such as pregnant and breastfeeding women, children and adolescents and patients with a personal or family history of mental illness. Monica's case has been withdrawn pending further investigation. She hopes that one day the law may be changed.

Monica: The thing that concerns me is that particular law that obstructs people’s rights to choose how they experience their own consciousnesses.

She and Johan Bester, her attorney do not believe in one-size fits all approach.

Attorney: I think I should just make mention that the drug and drug trafficking act serves a very important and legitimate purpose in as far as it seeks to curtail the use of dependence producing substances. We have a drug problem in South Africa that is absolutely rife.

Johan believes there is a vast difference between a drug such as crystal methamphetamine and psilocybin - as does Monica.

Attorney: People love the work that she does and I think in as far as the law would suggest that her engaging in these practices makes her criminal, needs to change.

Dr. West believes that psilocybin, should, be administered in medically supervised settings for research purposes.

Dr. West: So the non-medical use of psilocybin can result in consequences and it happened to that old chap that wondered away and has led her being in this situation.

Soon after her arrest the elderly man tried to have the case against Monica withdrawn. Ultimately she is prepared to go to jail for her beliefs ………..
